newsitem.title: FRANCE: Shell France prepares output cut at Berre refinery.
newsitem.headline: Shell France prepares output cut at Berre refinery.

text.p: Royal Dutch/Shell plans to cut production by around 20 to 30 percent at its Berre refinery in southern France from Thursday if a blockade by striking truck drivers is not resolved, a plant official said on Wednesday.
Cutbacks at the oil and petrochemicals complex will be gradual and will vary from unit to unit, but the overall reduction will be between 20 and 30 percent, he said.

The contingency plan has been drawn up mainly because of problems getting deliveries into the 127,000 barrels per day refinery through a truckers' blockade, rather than the problem of storing unsold products.
"We are not getting supplies of chemicals," the official said.
Storage tanks at the plant were relatively empty following a maintenance shutdown last month but operators nevertheless saw no reason to fill them up unnecessarily, he said.
Some specialist units -- like a polyethylene unit which shut down to deal with a technical hitch this weekend and has been left idle -- may be closed during the dispute, he said.
But he stressed the refinery was working normally for now and there was no immediate threat of shutdown.

Other refineries in the region also faced possible output cuts of the same magnitude, he said. There was no immediate confirmation from the other three or four major plants in the area, Europe's largest Mediterranean refining centre.
Oil industry association UFIP said earlier, however, that southern refineries were at risk from production cuts.
The Berre official said there was no petrol in any nearby filling stations. Truckers were running flexible blockades with just a few cars or lorries but were well organised with radios.
